references.text: God's promise to Abraham of the land stretching from the River of Egypt to the Euphrates, mentioning the same nations that are to dwell there.
Reiteration of the promise to bring the people out of Egypt into the land of the Canaanites, a land flowing with milk and honey.
The fulfillment of the promise to bring Israel into the land flowing with milk and honey.
God promises to send an angel ahead of the people and drive out the same nations, into a land flowing with milk and honey.
The spies confirm that the land truly flows with milk and honey.
Moses reminds the people of God's promise to give them the land of the Amorites.
The promise of a land flowing with milk and honey is repeated as motivation for obedience.
The seven nations that Israel is to drive out are mentioned, including the same ones listed in Exodus 3:8.
Confession that God brought the people into a land flowing with milk and honey.
Joshua reminds the people that God drove out the mentioned nations before them.
Nehemiah confesses that God saw the suffering of their ancestors in Egypt, heard their cry, and promised to give them the land of the Canaanites.
Jeremiah calls the promised land a land flowing with milk and honey.
Ezekiel describes the promised land as a jewel among all lands, flowing with milk and honey.
Stephen quotes this verse in his speech and describes God's plan to deliver Israel from Egypt.
Abraham's faith in the promise of the promised land is mentioned as an example of faith.
Uses the promise from 3:8 as a contrast to explain why the first generation was denied entry.
